message.content:
This is a women's sweater of knit fabric with mixed fibers. Polyester is 50%, the largest single fiber by weight, so the garment falls under "other textile materials" (man-made fibers), heading 6110.30 (of man-made fibers). The fiber content, though, includes cotton 30%, nylon 10%, viscose 5%, linen 3% and metallic 2%. Since polyester is 50% and the other man-made fibers (nylon, viscose, metallic) total 17%, man-made fibers together are 67%. This outweighs cotton at 30%, so the predominant fiber by weight is man-made fiber, which classifies under 6110.30.

The stitch count note (fewer than 9 stitches per 2 cm) is relevant to the subheading for sweaters of 6110.30.30 (other, women's) vs. a different stitch-based provision. For 6110.30, the subheadings are: 6110.30.10 (sweaters, containing 23% or more of leather), 6110.30.15 (other, sweaters, containing 23% or more of leather...), 6110.30.20 (Sweaters, other, containing 70% or more by weight of silk? no...). Looking at the HTS: 6110.30.10 is "Sweaters and pullovers, containing 23% or more by weight of leather"; 6110.30.20 is "Other: Sweaters, vests... Sweaters and pullovers; Other: Containing 36% or more by weight of flax..." etc. The relevant one is 6110.30.30 "Other: Sweaters and pullovers, Women's or girls'": 6110.30.30 is "Other: Sweaters and pullovers: Women's or girls'", and 6110.30.3053 is the statistical suffix for women's sweaters. The stitch count is not a deciding factor in the 6110.30 subheadings. Since flax is only 3%, the 36% flax provision does not apply. The 6110.30.30 line has a 32% duty rate, and its statistical suffix for women's or girls' sweaters is 6110.30.3059 (other).

The most applicable code is 6110.30.3059.
